units.translation: 162-63. περὶ δέ σφιν ἰαίνετο: the shore was spread out, hyperbolically, inasmuch as Orpheus is said to charm even lifeless things. They sang a victory song to Apollo. "Therapnaean" means the Laconian, from a part; for Therapnae is a place in Sparta; some say a city, others a sacred place of Apollo.
165. ἐκ περάτων: from the bounding hemisphere. Lg (P)

168a. ἀνὰ Βόσπορον ἰθύνοντο: the distance from Byzantium to Chalcedon is . . stades, and it is called Bosporus because Io, being a cow, is thought to have crossed this place, passing from Asia into Europe, or because all narrow straits are called bospori. Some say that those dwelling at the mouth in ancient times, whenever they wished to cross to the other side, made rafts and yoked oxen and crossed over on them, whence the sea was named. There is also another Bosporus, of Scythia, called Cimmerian because the Cimmerians, a Scythian people, dwelt around those regions. Others say that the mouth of Lake Maeotis is narrow and long, resembling the Bosporus at Byzantium.

b. The story about the Bosporus is told differently by the ancients. Nymphis (fg 18 M. III 16) says that †Acarion† records that the Phrygians, wishing to sail across the strait, built a ship having a carved prow in the shape of a bull — just as Phrixus sailed on a ram-prowed vessel — and after they crossed, from the appearance

of the ship's figurehead the sea was called Bosporus. Ephorus (70 fg 156 J.) says that Io was abducted by Phoenicians and taken to Egypt, and in return for her the king of the Egyptians sent a bull to Inachus, and the place through which those carrying the bull sailed was called Bosporus; and after that bull died they went around showing the bull to everyone, since previously they did not know the animal. There are two Bospori, the Cimmerian and the Thracian, formerly called Mysian.
169. ἠλιβάτῳ: from which one can miss the base, that is, lofty and inaccessible. Lg (P)
170. ἐπαΐσσοντι: instead of "about to rush upon". Lg (P)
173-74. ἀλλὰ τό γ᾽ ἔμπης: but although the wave is so great and furious, it is made smooth, if it meets with a good helmsman.
